topic.title: Hiking 03 - shifting constraints, a revived option, an ambiguous "sounds good"
topic.problem: Hiking 03 - shifting constraints, a revived option, an ambiguous "sounds good"
topic.decision_requested: Hiking 03 - shifting constraints, a revived option, an ambiguous "sounds good"

criteria.description: Destination should be close / low travel distance.
Destination should be affordable / low cost.
Budget cap: $2,000 per person all-in (agreed by all six participants).

proposals.title: Patagonia – Torres del Paine, W Trek
5-day trip to a closer destination (e.g. Banff) so all 6 can attend
Full 7-day trip (Nov 14–21) with Jordan joining for the first 5 days only

claims.statement: The Dolomites needs six or seven days to do properly.
Flights to Patagonia cost approximately $1,300 per person.
In mid-November Banff is hit or miss; many trails are under snow.
Zion canyon in mid-November is usually in the 60s°F and sunny, with very few crowds.
Zion, Bryce Canyon, and Snow Canyon are all within a couple of hours of each other.
W Trek refugios cost approximately $600 per person. Combined with ~$1,300 flights, total is approximately $1,900, leaving ~$100 for other costs.
Calgary round-trip flights found for $380 per person.
A lodge in Canmore is available at $90 per night. Jordan estimates Banff could come in well under $2,000 per person all-in.
The lower trails around Canmore stay walkable in November.
Banff temperatures in November are around 20°F.
The Narrows at Zion in November is empty and gorgeous, though on some days it may be too cold to wade.

arguments.statement: Patagonia is not worth the long flight for only five days.
The Dolomites needs 6–7 days, so a 5-day window does not work for it either.
At a $2,000 budget, Patagonia flights alone (~$1,300) leave almost nothing for accommodation and food.
Banff in mid-November is hit or miss; many trails may be snow-covered.
Zion in mid-November is typically 60s°F, sunny, and uncrowded.
Zion, Bryce, and Snow Canyon are all within a couple of hours, providing a full week of hiking.
Combining Zion, Bryce, and Snow Canyon makes it a road trip rather than a proper hiking trip.
Flights (~$1,300) + refugios (~$600) = ~$1,900, so Patagonia technically fits within $2,000, albeit very tightly.
After flights and refugios (~$1,900), only ~$100 remains for food, buses, and gear — insufficient.
Skipping gear rental and cooking own food could bring Patagonia within the $2,000 budget.
If participants need to skip gear rental and self-cater, Patagonia is a 'stretch trip', not a budget trip.
Calgary flights at $380 RT + Canmore lodge at $90/night means Banff could come in well under $2,000.
Banff in November means snowshoeing, not hiking.
Lower Canmore trails stay walkable in November, and snowshoeing is a valid activity.
Zion's November temperatures (~60s°F) are much more comfortable than Banff's (~20°F) for hiking.
Banff is beautiful in winter and offers ice walks and hot springs as additional activities.
Zion is essentially the same as Yosemite — comfortable and close but not a special or distinctive hiking destination.
Zion is special; The Narrows in November is empty and gorgeous.

positions.statement: Alex wants Patagonia / Torres del Paine W Trek.
Jordan wants Banff because it is close and cheap.
Maya suggests Yosemite as cheap and easy.
Leo wants Zion; says Utah in November is underrated.
Sam is OK with $2,000 if everyone else agrees.
Jordan accepts $2,000 per-person budget; notes it suits Banff well.
Alex accepts $2,000 budget but notes it nearly eliminates Patagonia given ~$1,300 flights.
Maya prefers Zion over Yosemite for November and is happy to drop Yosemite if Zion stays.
Alex prefers Patagonia or the Dolomites over Zion.
Priya is not against reopening Banff but acknowledges Alex's concern about hiking quality in November.
Maya thinks Patagonia is basically out because it cannot fit within the $2,000 budget.
Alex insists Patagonia is not out — it is tight but still feasible within $2,000.

Five participants available Nov 14–21; Jordan only available Nov 14–18. Whether to do 5 days or 7 days (and whether Jordan attends part of a longer trip) is unresolved.
Banff initially dropped by group consensus (Sam, Maya, Priya, Jordan agreed) due to mid-November snow risk making hiking unreliable. Later revived — see unresolved-banff-revived.
Yosemite dropped from consideration. Maya (proposer) agreed to drop it in favour of Zion. No objections raised by others. Rationale: Zion viewed as better for November.
Open question: Does Zion area offer enough hiking content for a full 7-day trip?

Disputed: Alex says Patagonia is tight but viable within $2,000; Maya says it is basically out; Priya says the ~$100 remaining after flights and refugios is insufficient. Alex to price it properly (m070).
Dolomites flight prices and total budget have not been checked yet. Priya to research and report (m071).
Poll with all four options and prices is on hold until Jordan confirms whether the Nov 19 work commitment can be moved, resolving the 5-day vs 7-day dates question.
Action item: Alex to provide a full Patagonia price breakdown including flights, refugios, food, and transfers.
Action item: Priya to research and provide a full Dolomites price breakdown.
Action item: Jordan to (1) provide full Banff price breakdown and (2) check if the Nov 19 work commitment can be moved. Everyone waiting on this before committing to dates or running the poll.

messages.text: Time to decide the November hiking trip. Options, dates, budget. Go.
Patagonia. Torres del Paine, the W trek. It's the trip.
Dolomites, please. Huts and food.
Banff for me, it's close and cheap.
Yosemite? Cheap and easy.
I'd like to add Zion to the list. Utah in November is underrated.
Five options then. Dates first. I proposed Nov 14 to 21. Anyone blocked?
I can only do the 14th to the 18th. I have a work thing on the 19th that I can't move.
That's five days. Patagonia isn't worth flying to for five days.
The Dolomites also needs six or seven days.
Can the rest of us do the full week?
I can.
I can.
I can.
I can do the full week too.
I can, but I need to be home by the 22nd.
Ok, so five of us can do Nov 14 to 21 and Jordan can only do the 14th to 18th. Parking that.
Budget. $2,500 per person all in?
Fine.
Fine.
Fine.
Alex, Priya and Jordan are OK with $2,500. Maya, Leo?
Fine.
I'd be more comfortable at $2,000. Could we do that instead?
I'm OK with $2,000 if everyone else is.
$2,000 works for me.
$2,000 is fine, it's easier for Banff anyway.
$2,000 works.
Fine with $2,000, but then Patagonia is basically out. Flights alone are $1,300.
Ok, so budget is now $2,000 per person all in. Patagonia is the one at risk.
Fair warning on Banff. Mid-November is hit or miss, lots of trails are under snow.
If Banff is snowy I'd rather drop it. Any objections?
Fine with dropping Banff.
Drop it, I think.
Ok, dropping Banff. It was my suggestion anyway.
Good, less to argue about.
Now Zion. Mid-November is usually in the 60s and sunny in the canyon, and there's hardly any crowds.
Zion sounds great. Better than Yosemite for November, so I'm happy dropping Yosemite if Zion stays.
Are there enough hikes for a full week though?
Yes. Zion, Bryce and Snow Canyon are all within a couple of hours of each other.
That's a road trip more than a hike trip. I'd rather do Patagonia or the Dolomites.
Alex, Patagonia is over budget on flights alone though.
Flights are $1,300 and the W trek refugios are about $600. That's $1,900. Tight but it fits.
That leaves $100 for food, buses and gear. It doesn't fit.
I'd skip the gear rental and cook my own food. It can work.
Then it's not a budget trip, it's a stretch trip.
While we're on budgets, I just found Calgary flights for $380 round trip.
And a lodge in Canmore at $90 a night. Banff might come in well under $2,000 with money to spare.
Ok that's very tempting. Maybe I want Banff back on the list.
Banff in November isn't hiking. It's snowshoeing.
The lower trails around Canmore stay walkable. And snowshoeing counts.
I'm fine reopening Banff if people want it.
I'm not against it, but Alex has a point about the hiking.
What if we do just 5 days somewhere closer like Banff so I can be there for all of it?
Or we do the full 7 days somewhere else and Jordan joins for part of it?
Sounds good.
Leo, sounds good to which one, the 5-day Banff or the split trip?
Ha, honestly both. I'm fine either way.
Weather-wise, Zion in the 60s sounds nicer than Banff at 20°F for a week.
You'd layer up, but Banff is beautiful. And there are ice walks and hot springs.
Zion is the same idea as Yosemite. Comfortable, close, not special.
Zion is special. The Narrows in November is empty and gorgeous. Too cold to wade some days though, honestly.

Let me try to summarize. Budget is $2,000. Dates are Nov 14 to 21 for five of us, Jordan is limited to the 14th to 18th. Options are Patagonia, Dolomites, Banff (Jordan reopened it) and Zion. Yosemite is dropped. Right?
Yes, but I think Patagonia is basically out on budget.
Not out. Tight.
I'd also like to check the Dolomites budget. I haven't looked at flights yet.
The summary is right.
Yes.
Ok. Let's do a poll tomorrow night with all four options and a price for each.
I'll price Patagonia properly, including food and transfers.
I'll price the Dolomites.
I'll price Banff, and check if I can move my work thing.
I'll price Zion.
I'll build the comparison sheet.
The dates question should be settled before the poll though. 5 days or 7.
Agree. Let me see if I can move the work thing before you all commit.
Good, thanks Jordan.
Ok, then we wait for Jordan's answer on dates before the poll.
Sounds good.
Works for me.
